rows.evidence: Q1: Section 4/4.1 and Figures 7-8 - the authors describe a prototype (Node.js server, five virtual blockchain nodes, Arduino/NodeMCU sensor nodes) and report real-time sensor monitoring from two fields and the average response time of the system as their own experimental analysis.
rows.notes: The study is a system-design/prototype paper. Its only reported results are sensor readings (soil humidity, temperature, irrigation level, litres of water used/left) and the average response time of the IoT-blockchain system (Figure 8). It does not measure trust, security of data sharing, coordination or water sharing among farmers or communities; the statements that blockchain supports trust among community members are assertions in the abstract, Section 2.3.2 and the conclusion, not findings. The data availability statement even says no new data were created or analysed, so Q1 is a borderline 'yes'. The water-use measurement is a water-level sensor reporting litres used rather than flow metering as such, but this is close enough not to flag a mismatch. The study only demonstrates that such a system can be built (a precondition), hence upstream.

rows.evidence: Q1: Section 4.1 and Figures 7-8 - prototype implementation with Arduino-based humidity, temperature and water-level sensors, five virtual blockchain nodes, and an evaluation of average response time versus number of irrigation indices executed.
rows.notes: The study reports no result on water-use efficiency or water savings. Figure 7d only displays litres of water used and amount left as a monitoring output; there is no comparison against a baseline, no quantification of water saved or efficiency gained, and the sole performance indicator evaluated is average response time (Figure 8). The claim that the system 'maximises the efficiency of water use' is not tested. Monitoring of water use is at most a precondition for conservation, so upstream is set. Q1 is borderline: the data availability statement says no new data were created or analysed, and the figures appear largely illustrative.

notes: Full text appears complete. The paper is primarily a conceptual architecture (EBMA-IoT) with a lightly described prototype; experimental content is limited to real-time sensor plots from two fields and an average response-time curve, with no statistics, dispersion measures, stated limitations, or multi-site evaluation. Neither social (trust/coordination) nor water-efficiency effects are measured.
